thread:
alex: Ran nvprof + nvvp on kv-cache-rewrite branch, got a surprise: SparseAttentionV2_stage1 is eating ~48% GPU time in the tail workloads. timeline attached, nvprof kernel summary below. looking for quick triage pointers

alex: nvprof --print-gpu-trace --metrics all ./bin/server --profile-mode
```
GPU activities:
  Time(%)      Time    Calls       Avg       Min       Max  Name
  48.2%    12.34s       456   27.1ms    0.45ms   210.34ms  SparseAttentionV2_stage1
  15.9%     4.07s      1024    3.9ms    0.20ms    45.2ms   KVCache_prefetch
  10.5%     2.69s       890    3.0ms    0.12ms    60.5ms   ContinuousBatcher_merge
   8.0%     2.05s       302    6.8ms    0.80ms    42.0ms   Softmax_kernel_v4
   ...
```

kevin: nice catch. do we have an occupancy / achieved_occupancy snapshot? large max times on SparseAttention look like serialization + low SM utilization. can you dump SASS or use nsys to get sm_efficiency?

maria: also check batch size histogram — if heuristics pushed lots of size-1 requests, attention kernels will hit low occupancy and blow up. perfetto/nvsight timeline would show per-kernel queues.

alex: batch histogram: most requests are size 1-3 after the optimizer change; median=2, p95=8. kv-prefetch frequency went up too because p99 lat spikes triggered prefetches.

sara: are KV cache evictions thrashing? if prefetch runs concurrently with attention, could be warp contention + extra mem ops. eviction log tail?

alex: eviction log snippet:
```
[evict] ts=2109876541.123 id=abc123 bucket=7 reason=memory_pressure live_keys=48000
[fetch] ts=2109876541.125 id=abc124 prefetch_ok latency=1.2ms
[evict] ts=2109876541.129 id=abc125 bucket=7 reason=checkpoint
```

kevin: hmm. two theories: 1) SparseAttention kernel is running with small seq_len + small batch => poor multiprocessor occupancy; 2) KV prefetch introduces additional memcpy + L2 thrash that spiders into attention kernel runtime. we should check achieved_occupancy and dram_utilization.

maria: please re-run with nsys capture: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --ms 5000 --output=nvstmp ./bin/server --config=...  and request metrics: sm_efficiency, achieved_occupancy, dram_utilization, flop_count_sp. that'll show if kernels are compute- or memory-bound. perfetto for long tail timeline (30s) would show overlap with prefetch.

perf-bot: Trace uploaded: https://internal-artifacts/trace/2109876543/nvstmp.qdrep (5.4MB) :thumbsup:

alex: re-ran with nsys + metrics attached. quick findings: SparseAttentionV2_stage1 achieved_occupancy=24% (GPU arch A100), sm_efficiency=31%, dram_util=62%. KVCache_prefetch shows many small memcpy asyncs overlapping attention.

kevin: 24% occ on A100 is low for an attention kernel. look into threadblock size / kernel launch config. do we have kernel parameters for SparseAttentionV2_stage1? shared mem usage?

alex: launch config from PTX wrapper: <<<grid=(g,1,1), block=(128,1,1), smem=48000>>>  (g varies by batch)

maria: 128 threads block + 48KB smem -> might be limiting active blocks per SM. try reducing smem per-block (split work) or increase block size to 256 to improve occupancy. also consider specialized kernel variant for small seq_len (micro-batched path).

sara: alternative: change batching heuristic to prefer combining small requests up to 8 tokens before dispatching. That reduces #invocations and increases average batch_size. cost: slightly higher p50 latency for single requests.

kevin: can we rank hotspots by two axes: total GPU time and low achieved_occupancy? i.e. produce a shortlist of kernels where time_fraction * (1 - occ_norm) is high.

maria: yes. I ran a quick script on the nsys CSV and got:
```
1) SparseAttentionV2_stage1  - time=12.34s occ=24%  score=0.937
2) KVCache_prefetch          - time=4.07s  occ=48%  score=0.211
3) ContinuousBatcher_merge   - time=2.69s  occ=35%  score=0.174
4) Softmax_kernel_v4         - time=2.05s  occ=60%  score=0.082
```
(where score = time_fraction * (1 - occ))

alex: very helpful. i'll try two experiments: A) quick kernel tweak (block=256, smem shrink) on a branch; B) bump batching aggregator threshold to combine up to 8 tokens and re-run perf tests.

kevin: also add per-kernel counters to runtime so we can see invocation distribution per model type + sequence length. that'll help avoid regressions.

maria: and add automated test that runs synthetic tail workload (many small requests) in CI with nsys-lite metrics assertion: achieved_occupancy >= 40% for attention kernels or else fail.

sara: schedule 30-min follow-up after you have runs? i'll be there to validate numbers.

alex: +1. created gh PR #5832 with kernel tweak + perf logs. will post CI traces when ready. thanks everyone. :rocket:
